components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The strongest recruiter-facing action, used for the resume CTA and any decisive next step.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;padding:8px 16px;border-radius:999px;border:1px solid transparent;background:var(--ios-blue);color:var(--ios-bg);font-family:Inter,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'SF Pro Display',sans-serif;font-size:0.8rem;font-weight:600;line-height:1;text-decoration:none;transition:transform 200ms ease,background 200ms ease,box-shadow 200ms ease,color 200ms ease;}.ds-btn-primary svg{width:14px;height:14px;flex-shrink:0;}.ds-btn-primary:hover{transform:translateY(-1px);background:var(--ios-blue-hover);box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(183,228,199,0.28);}.ds-btn-primary:active{transform:translateY(0);}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--ios-bg),0 0 0 4px var(--ios-blue);}

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The calmer follow-up action, used when the page should invite contact without shouting.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:8px 16px;border-radius:999px;border:1px solid var(--ios-chip-border);background:var(--ios-chip-bg);color:var(--ios-text-primary);font-family:Inter,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'SF Pro Display',sans-serif;font-size:0.8rem;font-weight:500;line-height:1;text-decoration:none;transition:transform 200ms ease,color 200ms ease,border-color 200ms ease,background 200ms ease,box-shadow 200ms ease;}.ds-btn-secondary:hover{transform:translateY(-1px);border-color:var(--ios-blue);color:var(--ios-blue);background:var(--ios-stat-bg);}.ds-btn-secondary:active{transform:translateY(0);}.ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--ios-bg),0 0 0 4px var(--ios-blue);}

components.css: .ds-tabs{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;padding:4px;border-radius:16px;border:1px solid var(--ios-glass-border);background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--ios-chip-bg) 86%,transparent);overflow:auto;}.ds-tab{flex:1 0 auto;min-width:max-content;height:32px;padding:0 12px;border:0;border-radius:12px;background:transparent;color:var(--ios-text-secondary);font-family:Inter,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'SF Pro Display',sans-serif;font-size:0.72rem;font-weight:600;line-height:1;transition:background 150ms ease,color 150ms ease,box-shadow 150ms ease,transform 150ms ease;}.ds-tab:hover{color:var(--ios-text-primary);}.ds-tab--active{background:var(--ios-blue);color:var(--ios-bg);box-shadow:0 8px 18px color-mix(in srgb,var(--ios-blue) 20%,transparent);}.ds-tab:focus-visible{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--ios-bg),0 0 0 4px var(--ios-blue);}

narrative.overview:
This portfolio should feel like a recruiter's private systems deck, assembled by the engineer himself. It is complete, confident, and softly cinematic, but never theatrical. The dark-first default matches the real viewing moment: a recruiter reviewing candidates on a laptop after hours, in a dim room, while deciding who feels credible enough to remember.

The mint accent behaves like a trusted systems signal, not a marketing highlighter. Glass shells behave like ordered drawers, holding dense information in calm modules. Warm brass exists only as a human note, enough to keep the page personal without weakening its technical poise. The light theme is a daylight counterpart, not a different brand.

This system explicitly rejects anything that reads AI-generated, generic, or template-driven. It should never feel cloned from a SaaS landing page, never drift into decorative glassmorphism, and never flatten Lowie's voice into a personality-free developer template. The craft must look owned.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, recruiter-legible surfaces with green-tinted neutrals.
One-sans typography system that earns hierarchy through weight, spacing, and scale.
Ambient glass depth, rounded utility pills, and calm motion.
Dense information broken into orderly modules that stay easy to scan.

rules.name: The Afterglow Rule
rules.body: Forest Afterglow carries actions, active states, and key numerals. If whole regions turn mint, the signal hierarchy is gone.

rules.name: The Warmth Rule
rules.body: Warm Brass is a humanizing accent, not a second CTA color. Use it where the page needs warmth, never where the page needs authority.

rules.name: The Single Voice Rule
rules.body: Inter carries the whole system. Contrast comes from weight, scale, casing, and tracking, not from adding a second display face.

rules.name: The Ambient Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth should feel like air. If a shadow edge becomes crisp, blue-gray, or obviously decorative, the surface is too heavy.

dos: Do tint every neutral toward green in both dark and light themes. Pure black, pure white, and neutral gray flatten the identity.
Do keep Forest Afterglow concentrated on actions, active controls, key numbers, and section eyebrows.
Do preserve the `24px` outer shell and `18px` to `20px` inner-module rhythm. The rounded system is part of the voice.
Do use blur, translucency, and ambient shadow only when they clarify hierarchy or grouping.
Do keep recruiter-facing copy compact, legible, and immediately scannable.
donts: Don't make it look AI-generated. If a new section could be dropped into any generic portfolio template, it failed.
Don't make it generic or template-driven. Avoid repeated icon-heading-text grids, canned hero metrics, or default SaaS landing-page composition.
Don't turn the glass treatment into decorative glassmorphism. Blur is structural here, not candy.
Don't introduce unrelated accent colors that compete with Forest Afterglow and Warm Brass.
Don't swap in decorative serif or editorial-magazine styling just to signal "design." This system earns personality through complete execution, not genre cosplay.
Don't use side-stripe accent borders, gradient text, or oversized rounded icons above every heading.
